Re: Q4 2019 Follow-Up Report - ApexHip MDR Trending per 2019-05-08 Correspondence

To Whom It May Concern:

Veridian Orthopedics submits this follow-up report pursuant to the timeline described in our correspondence of May 8, 2019 regarding medical device reporting and complaint trending for the ApexHip Metal-on-Metal Total Hip System, cleared under K162447.

For the reporting period ending September 30, 2019, Veridian’s review of post-market complaint data reflects an ApexHip complaint rate of 0.34%, based on complaints received relative to distributed units. The complaints continue to include reports of pain, elevated metal-ion findings, and revision procedures. Each complaint is evaluated individually by the Quality organization in accordance with Veridian’s complaint-handling procedures and applicable requirements under 21 CFR Part 820.

Veridian has continued its periodic trend review, including assessment of complaint narratives, available clinical information, returned-product information where available, and Medical Device Report determinations under 21 CFR Part 803. MDRs are submitted when the available information reasonably suggests that a reportable event has occurred. Follow-up information is submitted as appropriate when additional relevant information becomes available.

In parallel, Veridian’s engineering organization is conducting an ongoing evaluation of wear characteristics under a range of implantation conditions, including higher acetabular cup inclination angles. This work is intended to further inform our understanding of the relationship between surgical positioning, implant use conditions, and post-market observations. The evaluation remains in progress and is being reviewed through our established design and quality processes.

At this time, Veridian will continue enhanced monitoring of ApexHip complaints and trend information. We will report significant changes in complaint patterns, reportability assessments, or other information requiring notification to FDA in accordance with applicable regulations. We will also provide a further status update in the first quarter of 2020, unless material information warrants earlier communication.

Please contact me if FDA requires any additional information.

Sincerely,

Dana Okonkwo
Vice President, Regulatory Affairs
Veridian Orthopedics, Inc.

Veridian Orthopedics, Inc.
4400 Silver Lake Blvd

June 22, 2022

Northgate Health System
Attn: Risk Management / Materials Management
Re: URGENT — Voluntary Recall Notification
ApexHip Acetabular Cup, Lots V-2200 through V-2299
FDA Recall Number: Z-1418-2022

Dear Risk Management Colleague:

This letter serves as formal notification that Veridian Orthopedics, Inc. is voluntarily recalling ApexHip acetabular cup lots V-2200 through V-2299, manufactured at our Cork, Ireland facility between November 2021 and February 2022. This action has been classified by FDA as a Class II recall under recall number Z-1418-2022.

This recall was initiated after incoming inspection at two hospital sites identified flaking of the KinetiCoat porous titanium coating upon unwrapping of the sterile package, prior to implantation. Our investigation determined that a plasma-spray process parameter drift, following a chamber maintenance event, resulted in inconsistent coating adhesion in the affected lots. To date, 1,140 units from these lots have been distributed, with approximately 412 implanted.

We are asking that Northgate Health System take the following actions immediately:

1. Identify and quarantine all remaining unimplanted units from lots V-2200 through V-2299 in your inventory.
2. Do not use quarantined units for surgical procedures.
3. Complete the enclosed Effectiveness Check Response Form, documenting your inventory review, and return it to our Regulatory Affairs department within 10 business days of the date of this letter.
4. Contact your Veridian sales representative or Customer Quality at 1-800-555-0142 to arrange return and replacement of quarantined stock at no cost.

If any implanted patients have experienced adverse events potentially related to coating integrity, please report these through your standard adverse event process and notify our Complaint Handling department as well.

We regret any disruption this may cause and appreciate your prompt cooperation. Please contact me directly with any questions.

Sincerely,

Dana Okonkwo
VP, Regulatory Affairs
Veridian Orthopedics, Inc.
dokonkwo@veridianortho.com

Enclosure: Effectiveness Check Response Form

From: R. Delgado, Investigator, Office of Compliance, CDRH

Subject: FDA Form 483 — Inspectional Observations

[full text of the June 25, 2021 Form 483 transmittal letter, as previously circulated, quoted in full below]

RE: FDA Form 483 — Inspectional Observations
Veridian Orthopedics, Inc., Warsaw, Indiana Facility
Inspection Dates: June 14–18, 2021
FEI Number: 3003847215

Dear Ms. Okonkwo:

This letter transmits the observations noted during the inspection of your firm's facility conducted by the undersigned Investigator on the dates referenced above, pursuant to Section 704 of the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act. These observations are being provided to you at the conclusion of the inspection and do not represent a final Agency determination regarding your compliance. The following inspectional observations are made:

Observation 1: Records of complaint investigations reviewed for calendar years 2019–2021 did not consistently document the date of receipt of complaint information sufficient to establish whether reportability determinations under 21 CFR 803.50 were made within the required timeframes. Specifically, seven of twenty-two complaint files reviewed (TrackWise records) lacked documentation establishing when your firm became aware of information reasonably suggesting a reportable event, precluding verification of compliance with the 30-day MDR submission requirement.

Observation 2: CAPA record CAPA-2019-041, initiated in response to a 2019 coating adhesion issue, did not contain documented effectiveness check data or follow-up verification confirming that the corrective action taken was effective in preventing recurrence, as required under 21 CFR 820.100(a)(4).

Observation 3: Document control procedures for labeling revisions did not consistently reflect approval signatures and effective dates prior to release for use, as required under 21 CFR 820.40. This was noted for one of five labeling change records reviewed.

This Form 483 lists observations made by the FDA representative(s) during the inspection of your facility. They are inspectional observations and do not represent a final Agency determination regarding your compliance. Your firm should respond in writing within fifteen business days.

Sincerely,

R. Delgado
Investigator
Office of Compliance, CDRH

Re: Concerns regarding ApexHip metal ion levels in my patients

Dear Priya:

I am writing to request that Veridian review a concerning cluster of three ApexHip patients in my practice. All have presented with persistent groin pain and, in two cases, swelling and reduced function that is not readily explained by radiographic findings alone.

Serum testing has shown elevated cobalt levels in each patient, ranging from 18 to 25 ppb. Chromium is also elevated, although less consistently. The patients were implanted at different times over the past year, and I am in the process of completing additional imaging and workup. At present, I do not believe infection is the likely explanation.

The cup lot numbers available from our records are V-2039, V-2041, and V-2044. Please determine whether Quality has identified any complaint, manufacturing, or device-history concerns associated with those lots, or whether similar metal-ion reports have been received elsewhere. I recognize that three cases do not establish causation, but the similarity of the clinical presentation warrants a prompt look.

I would also ask that the review not be limited to lot history. If there is a broader design, bearing, positioning, or wear-related issue that could be contributing to elevated ion levels, I would like to understand what data Veridian has and what follow-up it intends to undertake.

One patient is likely to require revision, and I can make explant components and associated periprosthetic tissue available for analysis if that would be useful. Please advise regarding chain-of-custody requirements and the appropriate contact for specimen handling.

As a design consultant to Veridian and an early supporter of ApexHip, I find this personally concerning. I expect the company to investigate these reports carefully and communicate candidly about what is found.

Sincerely,

Dr. Marcus Feld
Atlanta Joint Institute

Minutes of Meeting

Time: 10:00–10:50 AM

Attendees: Tom Halvorsen (Sr. Design Engineer), Priya Raman (Director, Quality & Complaint Handling), Dana Okonkwo (VP Regulatory Affairs), Carlos Mendes (Product Manager, ApexHip)

1. Complaint Trend Update (Raman)

Priya walked through Q1 2020 TrackWise data. Metal-ion-related complaint volume (elevated Co/Cr, revision-for-pain, suspected ARMD) is now running 15-18 per quarter, up materially from the 2018 baseline of 3-4/quarter when the first Atlanta cluster was logged. Priya noted the increase tracks with growing implant population as much as anything, but the rate per 1,000 units in service is also trending up, not flat. She flagged this is consistent with what Tom's 2019 55-degree wear-test re-analysis predicted.

2. ECO-2019-118 Status (Halvorsen)

Tom confirmed the design change proposal (cup geometry / edge-loading mitigation) remains deferred per the 2019 design review decision. No new engineering work has been authorized since. Tom asked whether the updated complaint numbers change the calculus on revisiting it.

3. Discussion

Dana asked whether the complaint increase alone would trigger a design review reopening under our procedures; Priya said not automatically, but sustained upward trend plus registry data (NJR report expected later this year) could support it.

Carlos noted that 2020 is tracking to be Apex's best sales year yet — Q1 bookings are strong and the sales team is counting on continued momentum. He cautioned that any visible design-change activity, even internal, carries risk of leaking into the field and being read by surgeons or competitors as an admission of a problem, at a commercially sensitive moment. He was not opposed to engineering work continuing quietly but urged against any external-facing announcement or labeling change right now.

No consensus reached on reopening ECO-2019-118. Group agreed the complaint trend is worth continued close monitoring.

4. Action Items

- Raman to pull complete Q2 complaint data and re-run the trend comparison by mid-July.
- Halvorsen to keep wear-test analysis materials current in case design review is reopened.
- Group to reconvene after mid-year data to revisit whether ECO-2019-118 should move forward.
- Okonkwo to monitor for any external registry publications in the interim.

Dear Ms. Raman:

I am writing to formally log serious concerns regarding your ApexHip system. First, regarding the recent voluntary Class II recall notice we received dated June 14, 2022, my hospital's central sterile and incoming inspection team quarantined several components earlier this week. Specifically, an Apex acetabular cup from lot V-2247 showed visible coating delamination inside the sterile blister pack prior to presentation in the OR. The KinetiCoat porous surface was actively flaking off in small particulate fragments when the inner packaging was inspected.

This is unassisted flaking on unwrapping, which is completely unacceptable for an implant intended for immediate press-fit biological fixation. We have returned six unopened units from this lot to our local distributor per your recall instructions, but I demand an explicit accounting of what happened with your plasma-spray process and how this passed lot release.

1. Patient D.K. (DOB 11/14/1963): Primary left total hip performed March 2019 (Cup Lot V-1892, 54mm; Head Lot H-3112, 44mm). Patient presented at 38 months post-op with groin pain and severe functional decline. Pre-op serum cobalt was 9.4 ppb; chromium was 8.1 ppb. During revision on June 18, 2022, I observed extensive metallosis, fluid-filled cystic collections, and abductor necrosis consistent with ARMD. The cup was well-fixed, but significant edge-wear was obvious on the bearing surface.

2. Patient R.M. (DOB 04/02/1958): Primary right total hip performed August 2018 (Cup Lot V-1644, 52mm; Head Lot H-3088, 40mm). Revised on June 27, 2022. The patient exhibited a 6 cm pseudotumor displacing the femoral neurovascular bundle. Explant revealed gross blackened fluid and extensive soft tissue destruction. Tissue samples confirmed severe histiocytic response and metal debris necrosis.

Both explant sets have been retained in formalin per standard hospital protocol and are available for your engineering team to analyze. Please provide immediate TrackWise reference numbers for these adverse events and confirm receipt of this correspondence.

Re: Voluntary Recall Notification - ApexHip Acetabular Cup Lots V-2200 to V-2299
FDA Recall No. Z-1418-2022

To Whom It May Concern:

Veridian Orthopedics, Inc. hereby notifies the Food and Drug Administration of a voluntary Class II recall of specified ApexHip acetabular cup lots. The affected devices are ApexHip cobalt/chromium acetabular cups with KinetiCoat porous titanium coating, manufactured at Veridian’s Cork, Ireland facility.

The recall applies to cup lots V-2200 through V-2299, manufactured from November 2021 through February 2022. A total of 1,140 units were distributed in the United States. Based on the current lot-trace reconciliation, 412 units have been implanted. The balance is located in customer or distributor inventory, has been returned, or remains in Veridian-controlled inventory pending final reconciliation.

The recall was initiated following incoming-inspection reports from two hospital customers, including Northgate Health System and a Denver-area hospital. In each report, flaking of the KinetiCoat coating was observed upon removal of the device from its packaging. No other ApexHip lots are included in this action.

Veridian’s investigation has identified plasma-spray parameter drift following a chamber maintenance event at the Cork facility as the probable root cause of the coating adhesion failures. Review of applicable batch records, chamber data, and maintenance documentation supports this conclusion. The investigation remains open, and Veridian will provide supplemental information should additional findings affect the scope or assessment of this action.

Immediate corrective actions include: (1) cessation of distribution for the affected lots; (2) segregation and inventory reconciliation of affected product; (3) inspection and requalification of the plasma-spray chamber; (4) verification of plasma-spray operating parameters and associated monitoring controls; and (5) review and revision, as appropriate, of maintenance and post-maintenance release procedures. The chamber will not be returned to routine production until requalification requirements have been completed and approved by Quality.

Customer notification letters are being sent concurrently to all known consignees, with instructions to identify, cease use of, and return affected product. Veridian will conduct effectiveness checks and provide periodic status reports in accordance with FDA requirements.

This action concerns a coating adhesion issue and is not related to metal-ion wear or other field performance concerns associated with ApexHip.

Please contact me at (574) 555-0142 or dokonkwo@veridianortho.com with any questions.

Sincerely,

Dana Okonkwo
Vice President, Regulatory Affairs
Veridian Orthopedics, Inc.

ENGINEERING MEMORANDUM

Date: March 10, 2022
From: Tom Halvorsen, Sr. Design Engineer, ApexHip
Subject: Explant analysis summary - Whitaker case, lot V-2114

This memo summarizes Engineering’s visual and materials review of the retrieved ApexHip femoral head and acetabular cup from the revision performed by Dr. James Whitaker in Denver. The components were received at Warsaw on February 28, 2022, under return authorization RA-22-0317. The cup is identified as lot V-2114. Component identifiers on the returned head are consistent with the operative record supplied by Dr. Whitaker’s office.

The case materials indicate revision after persistent pain, elevated serum cobalt and chromium values, and imaging findings described by the treating team as concerning for an adverse local tissue reaction. I am not making a clinical determination from the device examination; that remains for the treating physician and Clinical/Quality. The observations below are limited to the returned components and associated debris sample.

Visual examination of the bearing surfaces found circumferential polishing on the femoral head, with the more pronounced damage localized to a band corresponding to the superior-lateral cup rim. The cup bearing surface has directional wear striations extending inward from the rim at approximately the 11 to 2 o’clock positions when oriented to the surgeon’s orientation marks. There is also a narrow area of matte discoloration and scratching at the rim transition. The pattern is not consistent with uniform, concentric articulation under nominal orientation.

The available postoperative radiograph supplied with the case file appears to place the cup at a relatively high inclination angle. Exact measurement should be confirmed by Clinical or the treating site, but the apparent orientation is in the range where edge contact becomes more likely.

This is materially similar to the pattern we saw in the 2019 55-degree inclination reruns. In that work, once the contact patch migrated toward the cup rim, wear increased substantially and the resulting head/cup surface damage was directional rather than evenly distributed. The retrieved surfaces here show the same basic mechanism: rim contact/edge loading followed by localized abrasive wear.

Materials analysis of the collected particulate residue identified cobalt/chromium-containing debris. Quantitation from the digestion sample was 18.6 µg cobalt and 7.9 µg chromium per gram of recovered residue. Those values should not be read as a direct measure of total in vivo burden, given recovery limitations and handling at revision, but the composition and relative concentration are consistent with the elevated serum ion readings reported in the case materials.

No coating delamination was observed on the accessible KinetiCoat exterior surface, and this does not appear related to the Cork coating issue associated with the V-2200 series lots. V-2114 is outside that population.

My conclusion is that the retrieval findings are consistent with the known edge-loading wear mechanism at high cup inclination, with associated Co/Cr debris generation. Quality should add this case to the cumulative metal-ion complaint dataset and include it in the next MDR trending review. I recommend retaining the components and microscopy images with the complaint file; Engineering has retained the raw photos and measurement worksheet in the Apex retrieval folder.

Tom Halvorsen
Sr. Design Engineer, ApexHip

MEMORANDUM

Veridian Orthopedics, Inc. — Quality Assurance

Date: August 15, 2019
From: Priya Raman, Director, Quality & Complaint Handling
To: File / Distribution per QA-SOP-014
Re: Quarterly Complaint Trending Summary — ApexHip, Q2 2019

Purpose

This memo summarizes complaint trending for the ApexHip system for Q2 2019 (April–June), per procedure QA-SOP-014 (Complaint Trending and Analysis).

Summary of Complaint Volume

A total of 11 complaints were logged in TrackWise for ApexHip during Q2 2019, up from 8 in Q1 2019. Of these, 7 complaints involved reports of elevated metal ion (Co/Cr) levels and/or early revision surgery, compared to 5 such complaints in Q1 2019. This represents a continued upward trend in metal-ion-related complaints over the last two quarters.

Complaints by region (metal-ion/revision subset, n=7):

| Region | Count |
|---|---|
| Southeast | 6 |
| Northeast | 2 |
| Midwest | 3 |

(Note: table totals to 11 as it reflects overall regional distribution for all Q2 complaints, not only the metal-ion subset; Southeast figure includes 4 metal-ion-related cases.)

Per record review, the majority of the affected implants trace to index surgeries performed in 2017–2018, consistent with prior quarters' pattern. Surgeon of record was identified in all cases; no single implanting surgeon accounts for a disproportionate share this quarter, though the Southeast region continues to represent the largest single source, consistent with Dr. Feld's practice volume in that territory.

MDR Assessment

Each complaint was individually evaluated per 21 CFR 803.50 reportability criteria. Per procedure, none of the seven metal-ion/revision complaints, taken individually, meets the threshold for mandatory reporting — none reflects a malfunction that would be likely to cause or contribute to death or serious injury if it were to recur, based on available clinical documentation at this time. Individual determinations are documented in the respective TrackWise records (TW-2019-0398 through TW-2019-0441, non-consecutive).

Trend Assessment and Recommendation

While individual complaints do not independently trigger MDR obligations, the quarter-over-quarter increase (5 to 7 in the metal-ion/revision category) is notable and, per QA-SOP-014 Section 6.2, warrants continued close monitoring going into Q3. I am recommending that this trend be flagged for consideration of a formal CAPA, given the consistency of the pattern across regions and the concentration of affected units in the 2017–2018 surgical cohort.

I also recommend coordination with Design Engineering (Tom Halvorsen) regarding the wear-testing findings at 55-degree cup inclination completed earlier this year, as several of the revision cases reference elevated inclination angles noted intraoperatively. A joint review may help clarify whether device-related factors are contributing to the observed trend, or whether this remains within expected variation for the surgical population.

This summary will be provided to Regulatory Affairs (D. Okonkwo) for awareness and to Post-Market Surveillance (G. Novak) for inclusion in the next registry data comparison.

Priya Raman
Director, Quality & Complaint Handling

MEMORANDUM

TO: Dana Okonkwo (VP, Regulatory Affairs), Rachel Steinberg (General Counsel), Dr. Leon Adeyemi (Chief Medical Officer), Marcus Lee (VP, Sales)
FROM: Carlos Mendes (Product Manager, ApexHip)
DATE: September 28, 2021
SUBJECT: Draft "Dear Doctor" Letter – ApexHip Acetabular System Labeling Update

Following the decisions reached during our September 14 Registry Signal Review meeting, I have prepared the initial draft text for the upcoming customer notification ("Dear Doctor" letter) regarding the ApexHip Total Hip System.

As agreed by the review team and executive leadership, Veridian will maintain active commercial distribution of ApexHip while implementing an immediate Instructions for Use (IFU) labeling update to address emerging registry trends.

Background & Signal Summary
The primary driver for this communication is data presented from the March 2021 National Joint Registry (NJR) 17th Annual Report, which identified a cumulative 5-year revision rate of 7.1% for the ApexHip construct, compared to an average class benchmark of approximately 3.2% across contemporary metal-on-metal (MoM) hip resurfacing and total replacement systems. While internal clinical evaluations indicate that well-positioned constructs continue to demonstrate strong clinical survivorship, registry data and internal engineering assessments correlate early revisions predominantly with adverse local tissue reactions (ALTR/ARMD) linked to elevated cobalt and chromium ion levels.

Proposed Letter Content & Labeling Guidance
The draft notification emphasizes patient safety, precise surgical technique, and targeted post-operative vigilance:

1. Patient Monitoring Recommendations: We advise clinicians to establish heightened routine clinical and radiographic follow-up protocols for all implanted ApexHip patients, with particular attention to individuals receiving larger femoral head diameters (≥44 mm). Routine cross-sectional imaging (MARS-MRI or ultrasound) and periodic blood metal-ion quantification (whole blood cobalt and chromium) should be considered annually or upon any presentation of unexplained pain, clicking, or swelling.
2. Surgical Positioning & Angle Inclination: Revisions strongly correlate with edge-loading phenomena. The revised labeling explicitly instructs surgeons to target an acetabular cup inclination angle within 40° to 45° and anteversion between 15° and 20°. Operating outside these ranges—specifically exceeding 50° of operative abduction—markedly increases the risk of accelerated fluid-film wear and premature component loosening.

Next Steps & Timeline
Our target mail date to all US and EU implanting orthopedic surgeons, chief medical officers, and relevant risk management personnel is mid-October 2021. Reps will receive accompanying talking points once this text is locked.

Please review the attached formal notification layout (`Apex_Dear_Doctor_Draft_v1.docx`) and provide your redlines. We require formal sign-off from Regulatory Affairs, Legal, and Clinical before Dana submits the final package to the agency and we proceed with mass distribution.

| Total recovered or otherwise accounted for | 728 |

All 1,140 distributed units have now been reconciled through documented implantation status, return, or customer-certified destruction. Recall effectiveness checks, including follow-up to non-responding accounts and distributor verification, reached a final effectiveness rate of 98.6% after reconciliation. The remaining 1.4% represents accounts for which receipt of the recall communication was confirmed through alternate records, including shipment, email delivery, and distributor contact documentation, but a completed response form was not obtained despite repeated follow-up.

The investigation concluded that the coating adhesion condition resulted from plasma-spray parameter drift following an October 2021 chamber maintenance event at the Cork facility. Specifically, the chamber was returned to production without adequate confirmation that operating parameters remained within validated ranges for application of the KinetiCoat porous titanium coating. Batch records and retained-sample review supported the conclusion that the issue was limited to the affected lot range.

Corrective and preventive actions were managed under CAPA-2022-0091. Actions included recertification of Chamber 3, revalidation of the applicable plasma-spray operating window, enhanced verification following maintenance activity, revised maintenance-release documentation, and tightened process-control review requirements for coating runs. Quality has verified implementation and effectiveness of these actions. CAPA-2022-0091 is now closed.

Regulatory Affairs recommends that the FDA District Office be notified that recall effectiveness activities and final reconciliation are complete, with closure requested for Recall No. Z-1418-2022. Recall records, including customer notifications, response records, distribution and return reconciliation, investigation materials, CAPA documentation, and FDA correspondence, should be retained in accordance with 21 CFR 806.20. The DHF-linked recall file should be archived in Agile with cross-references to the Cork manufacturing investigation and CAPA-2022-0091.

Dana

1. Individual Event Assessment: While individual complaint investigations continue to conclude that single-event MDR thresholds are not met in isolation (given ambiguous clinical etiology and unconfirmed revision attribution), the statistical accumulation cannot be disregarded.

3. Inspectional Exposure: Recall that we received an Additional Information request from ODE in May 2019 specifically questioning our trending velocity and signal detection thresholds. Failing to report an aggregate signal proactively leaves us vulnerable to a 483 observation regarding complaint trending timeliness during our next regulatory inspection cycle.

Devon, please prepare an initial draft submission package for my review, incorporating Priya’s TrackWise trend analysis as an appendix.

Dana

VERIDIAN ORTHOPEDICS
MEMORANDUM

TO: Commercial Operations, Regulatory Affairs, Product Marketing
FROM: Anika Shah, Director, Marketing Communications
DATE: March 20, 2017
SUBJECT: Claim Substantiation File – ApexHip Launch Materials (US Kickoff)
CC: Carlos Mendes, Product Manager, ApexHip; Dana Okonkwo, VP Regulatory Affairs; Dr. Leon Adeyemi, Chief Medical Officer

1. Purpose & Administrative Routing

This memorandum establishes the formal Claim Substantiation File (CSF-2017-004) for all promotional assets supporting the commercial introduction of the ApexHip Total Hip System at the April 2017 National Sales Kickoff in Dallas, Texas.

Per SOP-MKT-302 (*Promotional Material Review and Approval*), all collateral including sales visual aids, detail sheets, patient education booklets, and digital properties managed via Kessler Reid must trace every explicit and implicit product performance claim to verifiable engineering reports, clinical literature, or validated pre-clinical bench testing. Final collateral assets will be cataloged within the Agile PLM environment under change order ECO-2017-088.

2. General Regulatory Guidance

Following discussions with Regulatory Affairs (D. Okonkwo), teams are reminded that FDA 510(k) clearance (K162447, issued March 9, 2017) confirms substantial equivalence to the predicate device (ClassicHip) for commercial distribution purposes only. Under no circumstances should promotional text cite the 510(k) clearance letter as affirmative clinical evidence of safety, superiority, or long-term therapeutic efficacy. All field representatives and marketing agency partners must adhere strictly to cleared indications for use.

3. Promotional Claim Inventory and Substantiation Table

The following claims have been compiled from the primary launch brochure (P/N 093-4011) and the unbranded patient portal preview:

| Claim Text | Promotional Context | Primary Source Document | Review Status / Owner |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| "Largest head diameter for stability" | Sales aid, HCP web banner (ApexHip head offerings: 36–50 mm vs. traditional 28–32 mm) | ApexHip Engineering Specifications (DHF Section 4.2, Drawing Series H-3xxx); ISO 14242 wear-testing inputs | Substantiated. Engineering sign-off complete (T. Halvorsen, 02/2017). Comparative jump-distance data validated. |
| "Durable bone ingrowth through advanced titanium plasma spray" | Surgical technique guide, acetabular detail sheet | KBT Due Diligence Technical Dossier (March 2016); KinetiCoat Porous Coating Adhesion & Shear Testing (Report TR-15-088) | Substantiated. Porosity and mean pore depth metrics verified against KBT acquisition transfer files. Owner: C. Mendes. |
| "Engineered for active adults seeking return to motion" | Patient brochures, "Active Life" print advertising | Demographics market research; cleared indications under K162447 (non-inflammatory degenerative joint disease) | Substantiated. Appropriate qualifier language embedded in fair balance section. Owner: A. Shah. |
| "Designed to last a lifetime of movement" | Launch brochure cover tagline, trade show display headers, introductory video | N/A (Internal promotional concept / aspirational) | FLAGGED / PENDING REVIEW. See Section 4 below. |

4. Substantiation Exceptions & Action Items

Regarding the claim *"designed to last a lifetime of movement"*:

MarCom has flagged this statement during cross-functional review. While intended as thematic, aspirational positioning targeting younger patient demographics (45–65 age bracket), the phrase carries an implicit projection of implant longevity and long-term survivorship. Currently, Veridian possesses no prospective clinical revision-rate data, simulator wear data beyond 5 million standard cycles, or long-term registry tracking for the ApexHip construct to substantiate an explicit lifetime durability assertion.

This line is held pending clinical risk review and explicit written sign-off from Dr. Adeyemi. If Medical Affairs deems the wording poses excessive regulatory or compliance exposure, MarCom and Kessler Reid will modify the primary launch headline to: *"Engineered for a Lifetime of Movement"* or *"Designed for the Demands of Daily Movement,"* accompanied by appropriate survivorship disclaimers.

All final edits must be resolved before assets are sent to print on April 3, 2017.

Owen,

Per our discussion, I refreshed the Apex model using September actuals and the current field forecast. The model is intended to frame revenue exposure through FY24; it does not attempt to estimate claim severity or timing.

Apex FY22 is now expected to close at approximately $71.0M, versus the $96.0M peak in FY20. The decline began before the June cup recall in the underlying order data. The more pronounced step-down follows the September 2021 labeling update and what Sales characterizes as increased surgeon caution after the NJR data circulated. The recall remains a separate, lot-specific assumption in the model, although several field teams report customers are not making that distinction.

Summary output ($M):

| Scenario | FY22E | FY23E | FY24E | FY22–FY24 Change |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Status quo / current label | 71.0 | 62.4 | 60.1 | (15%) |
| Label-driven decline | 71.0 | 54.7 | 45.9 | (35%) |
| Full market withdrawal | 71.0 | 48.3 | 42.6 | (40%) |

The status quo case assumes current labeling remains in place, no broad commercial action, and modest attrition offset by existing account utilization. It is the closest to the current Sales operating plan, though I would not characterize it as the base case with high confidence.

The label-driven decline case assumes continued loss of new implanters, lower utilization among accounts that have moved Apex to a limited-use position, and increasing price concessions where distributors seek to retain volume. This case reflects the present trajectory in the Southeast and selected Midwest accounts more closely than the operating plan.

The withdrawal case assumes no new commercial placements after an orderly market action, with only limited residual revenue from contracted inventory and replacement requirements. This is necessarily a planning construct, not a recommendation regarding product status.

For reserve adequacy testing, I recommend using the full withdrawal scenario as the conservative revenue sensitivity. It produces the lowest contribution available to absorb claims-related costs and avoids relying on a recovery in surgeon confidence that we are not seeing in the current forecast submissions.

I have kept the $18M Q3 reserve as a separate line item in the workbook and have not assumed any insurance recoveries. We can walk through the account-level assumptions Monday if helpful.

Hannah

Rob, Owen, Rachel, Marcus, Carlos,

Please be advised that we have formally initiated a voluntary Class II recall with the FDA regarding ApexHip acetabular cups today, June 14, 2022.

Key details per our regulatory notification:
1. Scope: ApexHip cup lots V-2200 through V-2299, manufactured at the Cork facility between November 2021 and February 2022.
2. Distribution: 1,140 total units have been distributed commercially, with our current reconciliation indicating 412 units implanted to date.
3. FDA Reference: Recall number Z-1418-2022 has been assigned.
4. Root Cause: Investigation confirmed KinetiCoat porous coating adhesion failures (flaking upon package opening) caused by plasma-spray parameter drift following a routine vacuum chamber maintenance event in Cork.

Crucially, this recall is isolated strictly to the plasma-spray coating mechanical adhesion failure and is entirely separate from the post-market registry trending regarding metal ion wear and ARMD. However, given existing sensitivities around the Apex line, we anticipate that surgeons, hospital value-analysis committees, and potentially trade media may conflate these two distinct issues.

I have copied Marcus and Carlos so that Sales and Marketing can finalize field messaging immediately. We must ensure commercial reps have precise talking points emphasizing that this action is limited to the defined manufacturing window and coating integrity, rather than tribological performance.

Consignee notification letters and physical retrieval protocols will begin distribution tomorrow morning.

Regards,

Dana

MEMORANDUM

TO: Rob Castellano, Chief Executive Officer; Rachel Steinberg, General Counsel
FROM: Owen Park, Chief Financial Officer
DATE: October 26, 2021
SUBJECT: Preliminary Financial Exposure Note – Registry Signal Decision
CONFIDENTIAL / PRIVILEGED & CONFIDENTIAL WORK PRODUCT

Following our discussion last week regarding the September 14 Registry Signal Review meeting, I asked Hannah Berg to help model out our potential downstream exposure. As we finalized the path to maintain ApexHip commercial distribution supported by a labeling update and the upcoming Dear Doctor advisory, we need to understand the financial parameters should the registry trends in the UK (NJR) and domestic tracking (AJRR) fail to stabilize over the next 12 to 24 months.

Please note that this analysis is strictly exploratory and does not reflect a formal accounting position or GAAP accrual.

Scenario Modeling (FY 2022–2024 Outlook)

Our projections hinge on two primary variables: continued commercial volume and actual cumulative revision divergence against historical class baselines. At our current run-rate (~14,000 systems annually at ~$9,800 ASP), a continued divergence toward the 7.1% 5-year revision rate flagged by the NJR introduces predictable indemnity and defense tailwinds.

| Scenario | Modeled Revision Uplift | Est. System Volume (3-Yr) | Potential Claims Exposure / Reserve Range |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| Low Case | +1.5% to 2.0% over class average | 32,000 units (assumes tapering) | $8.0M – $11.5M |
| Mid Case | +3.0% to 3.5% over class average | 38,000 units (steady adoption) | $14.0M – $18.5M |
| High Case | +4.0%+ over class average | 42,000 units (aggressive growth) | $20.0M – $25.0M |

*Low Case* assumes our surgical technique labeling updates take hold, mitigating edge-loading outliers, with claims limited primarily to concentrated revisions and modest legal defense. *High Case* contemplates persistent ARMD and ion-related complications driving formal litigation across multiple territories, forcing substantial per-case settlements.

Recommendations

At present, ASC 450 (Contingencies) criteria for an accrual are not met; loss is neither probable nor reasonably estimable given the lack of active filed litigation and the uncertain causal link to technique versus manufacturing.

1. Maintain Current Stance: Do not book a formal balance sheet reserve for Q3 or FY21 year-end.
2. Quarterly Registry Monitoring: Finance should receive direct quarterly syntheses from Greg Novak's team to track NJR and AJRR curve inflections against these sensitivity bands.
3. Carrier Dialogue: Let us defer formal notifications to Aegis Specialty until Rachel's team identifies a concrete filed claim exceeding standard warranty resolutions.

Let's take this offline before the next Audit Committee prep.

Greg, Dana—

-----Original Message-----
From: Greg Novak <gnovak@veridianortho.com>
To: Priya Raman <praman@veridianortho.com>; Dana Okonkwo <dokonkwo@veridianortho.com>
Date: Mon, 20 Sep 2021 09:16
Subject: AJRR Q3 2021 data pull - ApexHip revision trend

Priya, Dana—

Following up on last week’s Registry Signal Review, I completed the Q3 AJRR pull using the same inclusion criteria we discussed: primary ApexHip procedures with at least 24 months of follow-up, compared with the available peer metal-on-metal cohort.

The AJRR data corroborate the direction of the March NJR findings. The absolute numbers are smaller and the confidence intervals are wider than NJR, but Apex is showing an elevated all-cause revision rate relative to peer MoM systems in the AJRR extract. The separation is most apparent in the 36–60 month follow-up band.

A few points from the stratification:

- The revision signal appears concentrated in the larger head sizes, particularly 44–50 mm. Smaller-head cases do not show the same degree of separation, although the case counts are limited.
- Where cup inclination was available in the registry record, revised Apex cases were disproportionately represented above approximately 50 degrees.
- That pattern is directionally consistent with Tom Halvorsen’s 2019 high-inclination wear work. I am not suggesting the registry establishes causation; it does, however, make the edge-loading hypothesis difficult to dismiss as a laboratory-only finding.
- Revision indications remain variably coded. Pain, elevated metal ions, adverse local tissue reaction, and “other mechanical” are all present, so I would avoid relying on any single indication category without chart-level review.

I have attached the summary workbook, including the denominator definitions, exclusions, and a tab showing the inclination/head-size subset. I also included the NJR figures for reference, but did not combine the registries analytically.

Please let me know whether you want the underlying case-level list routed to Quality for complaint cross-checking. My recommendation remains that we maintain a recurring monthly review through the label-update period rather than wait for the next annual registry publication.

Greg

Post-Market Surveillance Memorandum

Date: June 5, 2023
From: Greg Novak, Director, Post-Market Surveillance
To: File
Subject: Registry and complaint correlation memo - pre-MDL summary

This memorandum summarizes the relationship between external registry findings and Veridian’s internal ApexHip complaint and MDR trending through the current reporting period. I prepared this as a consolidated reference because we should expect requests for this material as the pending state-court matters develop and, potentially, are coordinated.

The short version is that the registry and complaint datasets have been directionally consistent since 2019. They are not interchangeable datasets, and neither proves causation on its own. However, both show a pattern of earlier-than-expected revision in a subset of ApexHip patients, with metal-ion findings, adverse local tissue reactions, and revision narratives that are consistent with a wear-related mechanism.

1. Registry findings

The March 2021 UK National Joint Registry annual report identified a five-year ApexHip revision rate of 7.1%, compared with a 3.2% class average for the relevant total-hip population. The NJR data have limitations: it does not provide complete patient-level laboratory values, surgeon technique variables are incompletely captured, and the product cohort is materially smaller than the aggregate comparator group. Nonetheless, the direction and magnitude of the difference warranted the September 2021 Registry Signal Review.

AJRR extracts received in late 2021 similarly showed an elevated revision signal for Apex relative to comparable contemporary total hips. The AJRR data were less mature than the NJR dataset at that time, and the confidence intervals were wider. The mid-2022 AJRR refresh did not eliminate the signal. Rather, it continued to show higher revision incidence in the Apex cohort, particularly in cases coded with pain, metallosis/metal-debris terminology, instability, or aseptic loosening. Coding practices vary by site, so these categories should not be treated as clinical adjudications.

2. Internal complaints and MDRs

TrackWise complaint entries first showed a meaningful cluster in 2018, including three metal-ion-related complaints from Atlanta-area patients treated in Dr. Feld’s practice. By 2019, the internal trend reports reflected increasing reports of elevated cobalt and chromium, pain, fluid collections, tissue reaction, and early revision. Not all reported cases contained complete records or confirmed implant component details. Several were initially coded under broad pain or revision categories before follow-up information was received.

The MDR population follows the same general trajectory. Reportable events increased as revisions and explant findings were received, although MDR timing should not be read as event timing because of reporting lags, supplemental records, and follow-up. The internal complaint/MDR trend is therefore most useful when reviewed by implant date and event date, where available, rather than filing date alone.

3. Mechanism assessment

The pattern is consistent with the edge-loading wear mechanism identified by Tom Halvorsen’s engineering team in the 2019 re-analysis of Apex wear testing. At 55-degree cup inclination, the testing showed approximately four- to six-fold increased wear relative to the standard 45-degree protocol. The clinical and registry data do not establish cup inclination for every affected patient, and patient, surgical, and implant variables may contribute. Still, elevated Co/Cr results and ARMD-type findings in the complaint records are directionally aligned with the engineering explanation and with the registry revision signal.

This conclusion is separate from the 2022 KinetiCoat cup-lot recall. The recalled V-2200 through V-2299 lots concern coating adhesion and a manufacturing parameter drift at Cork; they should not be combined analytically with the metal-ion/wear signal absent a case-specific basis.

Recommendation: Quality and PMS should finalize the Apex complaint database, including the current reconciliation of duplicate and follow-up records, and maintain a cross-reference between complaint/MDR records and the applicable NJR and AJRR citations. Any external response should clearly identify data-source limitations, reporting lags, and the distinction between the coating recall and the wear-related issue.

VERIDIAN ORTHOPEDICS, INC.
MEMORANDUM

Date: June 20, 2024
From: Owen Park, Chief Financial Officer
Subject: End-of-Period Financial Summary - ApexHip Product Line Closure

This memorandum summarizes Finance’s current view of the ApexHip product line through June 30, 2024, including historical contribution, withdrawal-related charges, and the contingent-liability outlook. It is intended as a closing-period reference for the product line; the underlying legal and claims matters remain open.

ApexHip was launched in the United States in April 2017, following 510(k) clearance, and in Europe in September 2017. It achieved rapid adoption in its intended active-adult segment and became a material contributor to Reconstructive revenue. The line reached peak annual sales in 2020, when approximately 14,200 systems generated revenue of approximately $96 million. That represented roughly 22% of consolidated company revenue for that year.

Based on booked sales through withdrawal and remaining recognized revenue, Finance estimates cumulative ApexHip lifetime revenue of approximately $410 million for the 2017 through 2024 period. This estimate includes U.S. and international sales and is subject to routine quarter-end revenue adjustments, returns, credits, and distributor true-ups. The February 2, 2024 voluntary market withdrawal ended new commercial sales activity, although certain post-withdrawal customer credits, field inventory returns, and service-related transactions continue to be processed.

The financial impact of ApexHip has developed in stages. In the third quarter of 2022, the Company recorded an $18 million reserve for Apex-related claims. At that time, the reserve reflected known and reasonably estimable exposure, including then-pending claims activity, anticipated defense costs, and available information regarding product allegations. It did not represent a final estimate of ultimate loss.

As additional claims were filed and the federal proceeding developed, Finance’s internal range increased. During 2023 and the first half of 2024, working estimates generally placed the potential Company-funded exposure in a range of $45 million to $70 million, depending on assumptions concerning case inventory, dismissal rates, indemnity allocation, defense costs, insurance recoveries, and the timing and structure of any global resolution.

MDL 3102 currently includes approximately 520 filed cases and continues to grow. Case count alone is not a measure of ultimate liability; however, the pace of filings, claimant medical profiles, revision status, and the cost of ongoing coordinated litigation have been incorporated into our reserve analyses. Finance will continue to coordinate with Legal, Quality, Regulatory, and our outside advisors as additional case-specific information becomes available.

For planning purposes, management is evaluating a proposed settlement contribution of $80 million from Veridian, combined with a tentative $40 million coverage contribution from Aegis Specialty. These figures remain subject to negotiation, policy analysis, allocation discussions, and agreement on a mediation framework. They should not be understood as a completed settlement, a final coverage determination, or a fixed accounting conclusion. Aegis’s participation remains tentative, and any recovery will depend on finalized terms and applicable policy conditions.

The total financial effect of ApexHip therefore includes more than the product-line reserve. It also encompasses withdrawal costs, customer credits, inventory-related charges, continuing defense expense, and internal support costs. Those elements will continue to be tracked separately where practical so that reserve movements are not conflated with ordinary operational closeout expenses.

Finance will continue quarterly reserve reviews until the mediation framework is finalized and all claims are resolved. Any material change in the expected Veridian contribution, Aegis participation, case inventory, or accounting treatment will be brought forward through the standard quarter-end review process.

Owen Park
Chief Financial Officer

From: Tom Halvorsen, Sr. Design Engineer
To: Priya Raman; Carlos Mendes
Subject: ApexHip concept design kickoff notes

Priya, Carlos —

putting down some notes from the concept kickoff last week so we have a starting point before design inputs get locked. this is early, still moving fast, expect changes.

Basic concept: total hip system, Co/Cr femoral head and stem (same alloy family as ClassicHip, proven manufacturing route), paired with an acetabular cup using the new titanium porous coating we picked up in the KBT deal. calling it KinetiCoat internally for now unless marketing wants something else (carlos - your call). the coating is the differentiator here, better bone ingrowth than our current sintered bead surface, that's the whole pitch for going metal-on-metal with this generation.

Target design inputs, draft:

- head diameters: 36mm to 50mm, in 2mm increments. larger heads for stability/ROM, which is a selling point for the "active" patient segment we keep talking about.
- cup sizes: 44mm to 62mm, matching head range plus offset options
- wear rate target: below ClassicHip benchmark (we'll pull the actual number from the ClassicHip DHF, I think Priya has that on file, need the polyethylene wear data as our comparator even though we're going MoM here, different failure mode obviously but leadership wants an apples-to-apples number for the design input doc)
- inclination range for cup placement: still nailing this down, but leaning toward specifying the standard 40-45 degree range surgeons are trained on. more on that below.

Open item — wear test protocol: we haven't picked a standard yet. ISO 14242 is the obvious baseline, that's what everybody uses and what FDA will expect to see referenced. question is whether we test at a single inclination angle or run a matrix across angles to see how sensitive the wear rate is to cup positioning in the OR, since surgeons don't all hit the same angle every time. I lean toward doing at least a sensitivity check but that adds time and cost to the test campaign. want to get Priya's read on this from a quality/DHF standpoint before I bring it to DR-2.

Timeline: aiming to have design inputs finalized and formally approved by September 2015. That gives us runway to hit DR-3 later this year for the wear test protocol decision and start locking down the coating spec with the KBT engineers (their due diligence notes mentioned they don't have a ton of long-term adhesion data yet, so we'll want to build that into our own verification plan rather than just leaning on their historical data).

Carlos — will need your input on head/cup size matrix vs. what sales thinks the market wants, and whether 50mm heads are overkill or a selling point.

Let's grab 30 min next week to align before I write this up formally.

Tom

Date: April 21, 2022

Location: Teams / Warsaw Hub, Conference Room 4B
Prepared by: Dana Okonkwo, VP Regulatory Affairs

Attendees: Dana Okonkwo, Priya Raman, Bill Kowalski, Rachel Steinberg, Carlos Mendes, Owen Park

Purpose
To review the KinetiCoat adhesion issue affecting certain ApexHip acetabular cup lots and determine the appropriate field action.

Discussion Summary

Mr. Kowalski reviewed Cork manufacturing records and the preliminary investigation. The affected population is cup lots V-2200 through V-2299, manufactured following the plasma-spray chamber maintenance event. The current evidence supports parameter drift during the relevant production period as the probable cause of insufficient KinetiCoat adhesion. The observed failure mode is coating flaking or separation identified on unwrapping during incoming inspection at two hospital customers.

Ms. Raman confirmed that the distribution reconciliation currently identifies 1,140 affected units distributed. Of those, 412 are recorded as implanted. The remaining units are believed to be in hospital inventory, distributor inventory, or otherwise pending confirmation through the effectiveness process. Quality will continue reconciliation as customer responses are received.

The group agreed that the product should be removed from distribution and that a voluntary Class II recall is warranted for lots V-2200 through V-2299. Regulatory will proceed on that basis, subject to final review of the notification package and lot list.

For avoidance of doubt, the scope of this field action is limited to the KinetiCoat adhesion/manufacturing issue associated with the identified cup lots. Metal-ion levels, wear performance, ARMD, registry data, and other metal-on-metal concerns were expressly noted as outside the scope of this action. Those matters are being addressed through their respective Quality, Post-Market Surveillance, and Regulatory processes and should not be characterized in customer communications as the basis for this recall.

Ms. Okonkwo advised that the target for recall initiation should be mid-June 2022, allowing time for completion of the health hazard evaluation, final lot tracing, customer lists, and FDA notification materials. Ms. Steinberg requested that communications remain factual and limited to the identified coating adhesion condition, the affected lots, and the customer instructions.

Mr. Mendes noted that Sales will require a concise field script and FAQ once the customer letter is approved. Ms. Raman stated that the initial hospital notification should instruct customers to identify, quarantine, and return unused affected cups, while providing a contact path for questions regarding implanted devices. No clinical recommendation language will be included without Regulatory and clinical review.

Mr. Park confirmed that Finance will begin modeling the anticipated reserve, including return logistics, replacement product, customer notification, and potential claim exposure. He asked Quality to provide a weekly update on the distributed/implanted reconciliation.

1. Dana Okonkwo — Draft FDA voluntary recall notification, health hazard evaluation, and associated Regulatory package. Target: May 6, 2022.
2. Priya Raman — Prepare hospital notification letter, distribution list, return instructions, and effectiveness-check process. Target: May 13, 2022.
3. Bill Kowalski — Complete Cork batch-record review and provide final affected-lot confirmation and root-cause documentation. Target: April 29, 2022.
4. Owen Park — Begin financial reserve modeling based on 1,140 distributed units and 412 implanted units; update as reconciliation changes. Target: May 6, 2022.
5. Carlos Mendes — Prepare draft Sales FAQ and field communication plan after Quality/Regulatory approve customer language. Target: May 20, 2022.

MEMORANDUM

TO: Dana Okonkwo, VP Regulatory Affairs; Priya Raman, Director, Quality & Complaint Handling; Dr. Leon Adeyemi, Chief Medical Officer
FROM: Carlos Mendes, Product Manager, ApexHip
DATE: September 20, 2021
SUBJECT: ApexHip System Instructions for Use (IFU) — Proposed Labeling Revision Rationale & Drafting

Following the consensus reached during the September 14 Registry Signal Review meeting, this memorandum outlines the commercial and clinical positioning rationale for the proposed updates to the ApexHip Acetabular Cup Instructions for Use (IFU-0144, Rev. D) and the associated Surgical Technique Guide.

1. Strategic Context & Objective
Recent registry publications (notably the 2021 NJR Annual Report indicating a 7.1% cumulative revision rate at 5 years) require clear risk-mitigation measures from the manufacturer. However, as discussed with senior leadership, our objective is to provide actionable clinical instruction to operating surgeons that accounts for these registry trends while avoiding an overbroad safety communication or market action that could inadvertently undermine commercial confidence in the Apex platform.

By framing wear performance around strict anatomical placement parameters, we can reinforce optimal surgical execution and address the underlying registry signal without triggering broader market alarm.

2. Proposed IFU Revisions (Section 4: Warnings and Precautions)
We propose adding the following language under Section 4.2 (*Implant Positioning and Wear Performance*):

> *"CAUTION: Clinical outcomes and bearing couple wear characteristics are highly sensitive to acetabular component orientation. Internal bench testing demonstrates that cup abduction (inclination) angles exceeding 45 degrees, particularly when combined with excessive anteversion, lead to localized edge-loading and significantly accelerated volumetric wear rates. Surgeons should verify intraoperative cup orientation using radiographic or navigational alignment aids to maintain an inclination target of 40° to 45°."*

Drafting Note: While this text directly incorporates findings from our internal bench testing regarding high-angle biomechanics, the wording intentionally characterizes this as an operative technique optimization rather than an inherent product limitation.

3. Surgical Technique Guide Additions
We will simultaneously issue an addendum to the ApexHip Surgical Technique Guide emphasizing:
- Verification of the "safe zone" (Lewinnek criteria) prior to final cup impaction.
- Specific warnings regarding patient anatomy variations (e.g., pelvic tilt in high-flexion activities) that can artificially elevate the functional inclination angle beyond 45°.

4. Alignment with Planned Communications
This labeling update will serve as the technical foundation for the upcoming "Dear Healthcare Provider" letter scheduled for release in mid-October 2021. By establishing that elevated wear is predominantly driven by component positioning outside the validated envelope, the communication appropriately shifts focus to surgical precision and patient selection.

5. Next Steps and Action Required
Per design change procedures, this revision will be routed under an expedited Change Order in Agile.

Dana — I would appreciate your formal regulatory sign-off on the proposed language above by Friday, September 24, so that Marketing and Regulatory can finalize the October Dear Doctor communication draft and confirm filing requirements under 21 CFR 803 / 820 before distribution.

I do not support “proven long-term durability.”

Sales growth and favorable anecdotal feedback from surgeons are not clinical proof, and neither substitutes for follow-up data. We have approximately 18 months of post-market experience, not long-term survivorship evidence. The design rationale may be sound, but that is a different claim.

Leon

CONFIDENTIAL MEDICAL COMPLAINT

4400 Silver Lake Blvd
Warsaw, Indiana 46580

RE: Formal Complaint – ApexHip System Early Revision (Patient Ref: RM-7104)

Dear Ms. Raman:

I am writing to file a formal complaint regarding a catastrophic failure of the ApexHip total hip system in a 54-year-old male patient whom I revised last week, exactly 38 months post-index procedure.

The patient presented with severe groin pain, persistent clicking, and joint effusion. Workup revealed markedly elevated metal ions, with serum cobalt measured at 18.7 ppb (chromium was 12.4 ppb). Intraoperatively, upon arthrotomy, I encountered profound metallosis with extensive soft tissue necrosis surrounding the abductor mechanism and a large pseudotumor extending anteriorly. The acetabular cup (54 mm) and femoral head (44 mm) showed obvious eccentric wear bands. The components were stable at the bone interface, but the local tissue destruction was severe enough to require extensive debridement and conversion to a constrained revision construct.

I specifically reviewed the initial postoperative films; cup inclination was 51 degrees, which is well within acceptable clinical placement for active patients. In speaking informally with several regional colleagues over the summer, I understand I am not the only surgeon seeing this pattern. Is Veridian tracking other reports of ARMD and accelerated wear with the ApexHip? Specifically, has your engineering team identified a design issue or edge-loading vulnerability with this cup at higher inclination angles?

Given the severity of the tissue destruction I observed, I expect a prompt and detailed written response regarding whether this event is being investigated under your CAPA system and reported to regulatory authorities. The explanted components have been decontaminated and retained per protocol.

Sincerely,

James Whitaker, MD
Denver Orthopedic Specialists
Attending Orthopedic Surgeon

AUDIT COMMITTEE OF THE BOARD OF DIRECTORS
MINUTES OF SPECIAL MEETING

Date: April 16, 2024
Time: 10:00 AM – 11:15 AM EDT
Location: Virtual (via Microsoft Teams)

ATTENDEES:
Committee Members:
- Arthur Vance (Chair, Independent Director)
- Margaret Holloway (Independent Director)

Management & Corporate Officers:
- Owen Park (Chief Financial Officer)
- Rachel Steinberg (General Counsel & Corporate Secretary)

External Audit Engagement Team (Deloitte & Touche LLP):
- Brian K. Sterling (Lead Audit Engagement Partner)

Recorder:
- Owen Park

1. CALL TO ORDER & AGENDA REVIEW
Mr. Vance called the meeting to order at 10:02 AM. Mr. Park noted that the special session was convened specifically to evaluate accounting treatments, accrual adequacy, and disclosure requirements concerning product liability exposure associated with the ApexHip system following the February 2024 market withdrawal and ongoing proceedings in MDL 3102.

2. REVIEW OF APEX RESERVE & MEDIATION SCENARIOS
Mr. Park presented an analysis of the current product liability reserve recorded on the balance sheet ($45.0 million, established and adjusted across FY2022–FY2023). Mr. Park reviewed modeling prepared by FP&A and legal defense counsel regarding upcoming court-ordered mediation tracks scheduled for Q3 2024.

Under evaluated settlement frameworks, initial bellwether resolution and broad inventory settlement structures suggest aggregate exposure significantly exceeding initial estimates. Management presented a recommendation to adjust the disclosed loss contingency range to reflect potential mediation funding scenarios.

3. INSURANCE COVERAGE DISPUTE (AEGIS SPECIALTY)
Ms. Steinberg briefed the Committee on the status of discussions with primary and excess carrier Aegis Specialty Insurance. Aegis previously issued a reservation of rights contesting the applicable aggregate policy limits, arguing that claims constitute separate occurrences subject to individual policy-year sub-limits, whereas Veridian contends the batch clause applies to consolidate aggregate limits.

Ms. Steinberg reported that Veridian has formally retained outside coverage counsel (Coventry & Dean LLP) to evaluate declaratory judgment options against Aegis. Given carrier resistance, management cannot treat disputed insurance proceeds as an asset offset under ASC 450 at this time.

4. 10-Q CONTINGENCY DISCLOSURE DETERMINATION
Following discussion with Mr. Sterling regarding ASC 450 accrual standards:
- The Committee concurred with management’s recommendation to expand the disclosed reasonably possible loss contingency range in the forthcoming Form 10-Q for Q1 2024 to $45 million to $70 million, pending preliminary mediation developments.
- Mr. Sterling confirmed external audit concurrence with this disclosure posture, noting that accrual beyond the low end ($45M) will depend on concrete settlement term sheets emerging from the mediation track.

5. ACTION ITEMS & DIRECTIVES
- Committee directed management to provide formal quarterly reserve sensitivity models and litigation status updates until final resolution of MDL 3102.
- Legal and Finance to submit a confidential memorandum on insurance recovery prospects prior to the July regular meeting.

ADJOURNMENT
There being no further business, the meeting adjourned at 11:12 AM.

Respectfully submitted,

Owen Park
Chief Financial Officer

DESIGN CHANGE RE-REVIEW MEETING MINUTES

ECO-2019-118 — ApexHip Acetabular Cup Design Change (Deferred)
Meeting Date: December 14, 2020
Location: Warsaw, IN — Engineering Conference Room B / Teams
Minutes prepared by: Tom Halvorsen

Attendees: Tom Halvorsen (Sr. Design Engineer, ApexHip), Priya Raman (Director, Quality & Complaint Handling), Carlos Mendes (Product Manager, ApexHip), Dana Okonkwo (VP Regulatory Affairs)

1. Purpose
Re-review of ECO-2019-118 (proposed cup/liner geometry change to address edge-loading wear identified in 2019 55° inclination testing), originally deferred at DR review in 2019. Meeting called to reassess in light of updated complaint trend data.

2. Discussion

2.1 Complaint trend data. Raman presented updated TrackWise trending showing a continued gradual increase in metal-ion-related complaints since the 2018 Atlanta cluster, with additional isolated reports logged from Denver and Nashville territories through Q3 2020. Raman noted the trend remains within historical variability per current procedure but acknowledged the slope has not flattened.

2.2 Wear test results. Halvorsen reviewed the 2019 55° inclination re-test data (originally reported in the Feb 2019 memo to Raman/Mendes) showing 4–6x wear at higher cup inclination angles versus the standard 45° protocol used for 510(k) clearance. No new bench testing has been performed since; data referenced is unchanged from 2019.

2.3 Cost of implementation. Halvorsen presented updated cost estimate for implementing the proposed liner geometry change. Original 2019 estimate was approximately $260,000. Due to tooling changes at the Cork facility since that time (new fixturing installed for an unrelated coating process change), current estimate has risen to approximately $410,000, driven by re-tooling and requalification of injection/machining tooling.

2.4 Registry data. Okonkwo noted the NJR annual report covering ApexHip's 5-year outcomes is expected in early 2021 and will provide updated revision-rate data relevant to this decision. Mendes agreed that this data would materially inform messaging and design prioritization.

3. Resolutions

3.1 The design change under ECO-2019-118 is again deferred. The team concluded that implementing the change at this time is not warranted given (a) complaint trend data remains within procedural thresholds, (b) increased cost of implementation ($410,000), and (c) the imminent availability of NJR registry data expected Q1 2021, which should inform the scope and urgency of any design action.

3.2 The team will reconvene promptly following receipt of the NJR report to reassess ECO-2019-118 in light of the new data.

4. Action Items
- Okonkwo to circulate NJR report upon receipt (Owner: Okonkwo)
- Raman to continue monthly trend monitoring (Owner: Raman)
- Halvorsen to hold current cost estimate on file (Owner: Halvorsen)

Next review: upon receipt of NJR data, tentatively Q1 2021.

Post-Market Surveillance — Interim Report

Report No.: PMS-2021-014
Date: June 28, 2021
Prepared by: Greg Novak, Director, Post-Market Surveillance
Product: ApexHip Total Hip System (all cup/head/stem configurations)
Distribution: Quality, Regulatory Affairs, R&D, Clinical Affairs (internal working file, pre-decision)

1. Purpose

This interim report summarizes post-market complaint trending for ApexHip metal-ion/wear-related events alongside external registry data from the UK National Joint Registry (NJR) and preliminary American Joint Replacement Registry (AJRR) figures, for the purpose of informing a cross-functional decision on next steps.

2. Complaint Trend Summary

TrackWise complaint records coded to metal-ion elevation, ARMD, pseudotumor, or related revision-for-wear categories show a sustained upward trend since 2019. Year-over-year, complaint volume in this category is up approximately 85% (2020 vs. 2019 baseline, annualized through Q1 2021 continuing the trajectory). This is not simply a function of increased implant volume — normalized against units sold, the rate per 1,000 implants is also climbing, not flat. I want to be careful here: TrackWise coding practices shifted somewhat in 2020 (see Raman's Q4 2020 coding audit), which may account for some of the apparent increase, but even a conservative adjustment leaves a real upward signal.

3. Registry Correlation

The March 2021 NJR annual report placed ApexHip's 5-year revision rate at 7.1%, against a class average (all MoM and non-MoM large-head hip systems combined) of 3.2%. That's more than double the comparator. I've cross-tabbed the NJR cohort dates against our own launch and complaint timeline and the divergence starts becoming visible in registry data roughly 3 years post-launch, which lines up reasonably well with when we'd expect edge-loading wear effects to manifest clinically if Halvorsen's 2019 high-inclination wear-test findings are operative in the field (see his Feb 2019 memo to Raman/Mendes re: 55° inclination testing, 4-6x wear vs. the 45°-only protocol used for original clearance).

AJRR data is still preliminary — we only have partial 2021 reporting — but the early read shows a similar directional trend for large-head MoM configurations generally, ApexHip included. I'd treat the AJRR numbers as corroborating rather than conclusive at this stage; sample size and reporting lag are real limitations. I'll have a fuller AJRR cut in the Q3 update.

4. Assessment

Taken together, I think we have three independent signals now pointing the same direction: internal complaint trending, NJR, and preliminary AJRR. Individually each has caveats (coding changes, single-registry limitations, immature data), but the consistency across three sources is, in my view, more than coincidental.

I'll also flag that ECO-2019-118 — the design change proposed by Halvorsen's team following the 2019 re-testing, and deferred at the time — has not been revisited since. Given the registry correlation above, I think it's reasonable to put that decision back on the table rather than treat it as closed.

5. Recommendation

I recommend the cross-functional group (Regulatory, Quality, Clinical, R&D, and Marketing) convene formally in Q3 to review this data package in full and determine whether labeling changes, a surgeon communication, or a design/manufacturing action is warranted. Given the trajectory of both the complaint data and the registry signal, I don't think this should wait until year-end review. I'm happy to present the full data set — I can also pull a more granular breakdown by cup inclination angle from surgeon-reported operative notes if that would help inform the discussion, though that will take a couple weeks to compile.

Attachments: NJR_2021_Apex_extract.xlsx, TrackWise_MoM_trend_2019-2021.xlsx

— Greg Novak
Director, Post-Market Surveillance

VERIDIAN ORTHOPEDICS, INC.
ENGINEERING MEMORANDUM

Date: March 22, 2021
From: Tom Halvorsen, Sr. Design Engineer
To: KneeFlex Design History File
Subject: KneeFlex Design Change ECO-2021-044 Summary

ECO-2021-044 proposes a process change to the porous coating application used on the KneeFlex tibial baseplate. This is a manufacturing-yield change. It does not alter the finished device’s intended use, material specification, implant geometry, packaging configuration, sterilization method, or performance requirements.

1. Background and rationale

Since January, Warsaw manufacturing has seen variable yield in the tibial baseplate coating cell, primarily driven by rejects at visual inspection for incomplete coverage at the posterior edge and inconsistent surface appearance in the medial corner. The current process uses a fixed fixture angle and a single-pass application sequence. Review of batch records and line observations indicates that part orientation during the final portion of the pass is contributing to uneven deposition.

ECO-2021-044 changes the fixture orientation by 12 degrees and replaces the current single-pass sequence with two controlled passes. The proposed settings are intended to improve coverage consistency and reduce rework and scrap without changing the released coating specification. The acceptance criteria remain those currently defined in KF-WI-217 and the KneeFlex tibial baseplate drawing package.

This is not a response to a field complaint trend. There is no identified clinical or product-performance issue associated with the current process. The action is being taken to improve manufacturing yield and reduce avoidable inspection rejects.

2. Proposed verification plan

Engineering will build three pilot lots using the revised fixture and application sequence. The pilot lots will be compared against three recent production lots manufactured using the current process. Testing will include:

- Coating thickness measurements at the standard mapped locations, including posterior and medial-edge locations;
- Visual coverage inspection per KF-WI-217;
- Adhesion testing on representative coupons and baseplate samples;
- Surface roughness verification;
- Dimensional inspection of the finished baseplate after coating; and
- Review of process capability for coating thickness and visual-inspection reject rate.

The verification protocol will define sample quantities before execution. Any result outside the currently released acceptance criteria will stop implementation pending Design Assurance review. Manufacturing Engineering will also confirm that the revised fixture can be cleaned and maintained under existing work instructions.

No new clinical evaluation is proposed because the device design and coating requirements are unchanged. Regulatory Affairs will assess the completed verification package and document the basis for determining whether a new submission is required. Current assessment is that this is a manufacturing-process change within the established design envelope.

3. DHF and controlled-document updates

Before release, the following records need to be completed or revised:

- ECO-2021-044 approval record and implementation checklist;
- Updated process FMEA identifying the revised orientation and two-pass sequence;
- Revised manufacturing work instruction and fixture setup sheet;
- Verification protocol and report;
- Training records for coating-cell operators and inspectors;
- Updated process validation summary, if required by the pilot data; and
- DHF index entry linking the ECO, risk assessment, test report, and released work instructions.

The change control package should make clear that yield improvement is the reason for the change and should not characterize current production material as nonconforming unless it failed existing release criteria.

For process consistency, the change-control package follows the same template used for prior ApexHip ECOs; that reference is to document format only and does not reflect any ApexHip technical evaluation or shared design issue.

I will circulate the draft verification protocol by Friday. Manufacturing needs to reserve the coating cell for the pilot run before the April preventive-maintenance window.

Tom
